listenings.text: Let me tell you what my week actually looks like. I am a partner at a mid-size firm in Chicago, and I work almost only with financial institutions. Banks, insurers, investment funds. Every morning I read what the regulators published overnight, because in tax law one single sentence can change a whole year for a client. Right now I am running three projects at the same time. The biggest one is a compliance review for a payments company that is growing much faster than its own controls. I build the projections, I test the scenarios, and then I sit in a room with the people who have to make the decision. That last part is the real job. Anyone can produce a number. Very few people can explain a number to a room that is nervous about it.

I run compliance for a European bank, and I hire external advisors almost every month. So people often ask me what I look for. It is not the longest memo. Honestly, I do not read the long memos. What I need is someone who can tell me, in two minutes, what the risk is, what the options are, and what they recommend. Our best advisor right now is a tax lawyer in Brazil. English is not his first language, and it does not matter at all. He speaks slowly, he uses simple words, and he stops when he is not sure. That is not a weakness. In a difficult meeting, that is exactly what a stakeholder needs. Confidence in this work is not about vocabulary. It is about being clear.

extra_audio.text: Good morning, my name is Leonardo Constantino. I am a partner at a law firm here in Brazil. I work in tax law for financial institutions. These days I am working on several tax reform projects.
